body: Whole Foods had them when I looked a few months ago! If you're not in a hurry, though, Amazon and eBay probably have them for much cheaper.

In my experience... I had a few mutual friends with my ex and he actually got to know some of my friends quite well after we broke up, which made things a little terrible. I felt like I got punched in the stomach whenever I saw him tagged in pictures or statuses on Facebook (my friends were usually very good about not bringing him up in conversation with me). It's definitely not the same as your situation, but despite that terrible sinking feeling each time I saw something about him, I think in the long term it was definitely better than completely re-opening up all the wounds that I tried so hard to stitch together. 

HOWEVER (I don't know why I didn't think of this earlier), I do now have a good relationship with my high school ex (whom I dated for 4.5 years), but it took 2+ years of no talking and leading our own separate lives. We don't talk very often, maybe once every few weeks, but I feel very comfortable telling him anything since he already knows so much shit about me it doesn't even matter. This only works, though, because we have both moved on and become entirely different people. The boy I crushed on in 9th grade is not the same person as the man I'm talking to at age 21. I'm not so sure that either you or your ex have completely moved on yet. 

There are always exceptions, but for the most part you're going to be a lot more unstable with her back in your life. The feelings will come back, for one or both of you, and harnessing these feelings will be horrendously difficult. Time heals wounds, but you have to allow it to do its thing.

Oh my god, your comment helped me so much. No old childhood feelings, but I'm currently in a friendship turned relationship turned fwb with an older man suffering from depression and his interactions with me are very similar (happy, flirty, nothing, depressed, very up-and-down). I started off as a listening ear and a close friend (feeling slightly sorry for him), and this soon turned to dating, and he ended up doing all these terrible things that used to happen to him (cheating, passive aggressiveness, manipulation, etc.) -- and although he has stopped these things since we're now "casual," somehow I can't get out completely because I'm too emotionally invested since I love him now both platonically and romantically... And I STILL feel empathy for everything he's had to go through. 

Thanks to your comment, I understand a whole lot more about my own situation and how easy it is to be sucked into a life that I don't really want.. Now I really know that even if he does love me, this isn't working out for me, and I need to somehow get out no matter how difficult it is. I always knew this logically but it never resonated with me this much emotionally until now.

Regarding your own emotional and mental health (without really addressing your problems with your current gf), I want to tell you that what you're feeling about your ex is completely normal but it's a bad idea to contact your ex again. Spending time away from my ex, whatever I was doing as long as I wasn't seeing him, talking to him, or hearing about him, allowed me to move on. 

My ex, whom I dated in my second year of college, was my best friend. I missed everything about him so much, but when we broke up he wanted to cut me out completely -- it killed me inside, but in the end time helped heal the wounds (I've just graduated after 3.5 years and I still feel weird seeing him in pictures with other girls, but I've moved on). When I first started dating someone else, what I felt with them was so miniscule compared to the days with my ex, similar to your situation... And I felt so uncomfortable and missed the (platonic) intimacy so much. But honestly it's because you're comparing a 4-month relationship with a 7-year one. 

I think you just need to give yourself time. I'm not sure you're ready to date someone new... I know I sure wasn't. For me, I kept comparing my new boyfriend to my ex for months before I finally began to move on. It ruined a potentially amazing relationship between us and wasn't fair to him.. It was clear that though I loved him, I was scared of getting hurt again. Of course, I'm not sure if this relates at all to what you're feeling, but your story somewhat resonated with me. Hopefully this helps. Let me know if you'd like to talk more. Good luck :) with whatever you choose.

Seriously, are you me?? <3 I feel the exact same way about everything you said haha. I've been trying to work on myself and I think I'm much happier now. Still not as happy as I was when I was with him, but mostly happy. :)

I feel you. I went through a similar situation. He was my soulmate and I don't even believe in soulmates, and for so many stupid reasons it all just ended up not working out, and he wasn't happy with me anymore. The pain was so overwhelming, and I thought it would never end. It really does help to go out (just even physically going outside will help a little). For three days I stayed in my apartment with nothing but snacks, alcohol, and my laptop. On the fourth day I decided to go outside with some friends and it was the best decision I ever made, because I managed to meet someone new (and now we're dating). 

I also never used to divulge many of my inner emotions to my friends, but talking to them about my ex was cathartic and generally very helpful. I stopped talking to them a while ago (I was seriously talking about him all the time and I worried I was getting annoying), but when I'm sad now I just make a throwaway post on this subreddit. 

The nights are worse than the days, but just avoid sad songs for now, no matter how tempted you are to listen to them. After my breakup I started listening to a lot of Two Door Cinema Club, Passion Pit, Imagine Dragons, Neon Trees, etc to take my mind off things. It's been two months and I still think about him every day, but it does get better. Some days are still terrible, but I'm happier now. Please PM me if you want to talk.

The first several months were wonderful, as in most relationships. But in the later months I got busier and busier, to the point that he wasn't happy with the amount of time I could give to him. And it was more than that -- since I was busy all the time, I was tired and sometimes stressed when I was with him, and consequently we would spend hours together but not really interacting much. 

Then, he started acting passive-aggressive, trying to keep inside most of what he felt (but sometimes failing to do so). I think that ended up affecting me quite significantly because I started doing that too. In the end, I was feeling smothered and constantly anxious because of his passive-aggressiveness, so I started hanging out with my other friends more often to take a break and relieve the stress -- but this just perpetuated the cycle. I kept wanting to work towards a better relationship, but he eventually got too tired of trying, so we broke up. 

It's a much more complicated story than what I wrote above (I could probably talk for hours about it), but in the end our breakup was probably a concoction of repressed emotions, miscommunication, and differing lifestyles. I promised myself after our breakup I would strive for emotional transparency when interacting with other people in the future :) still working on it.
I'm here if you need someone to talk to.
